title: How table tennis is run in England
seo_title: How table tennis is run in England: TTE explained
description: How Table Tennis England, the county associations, local leagues and clubs fit together, what membership buys and how England fits into GB and world sport.
summary: Table Tennis England sits at the top of the domestic game, with county associations, local leagues and clubs below it. Above it, England plays as itself at the World Championships but as part of Great Britain at the Olympics.
key_points: Table Tennis England is the governing body for the sport in England, a not-for-profit company based in Milton Keynes.
Clubs and leagues affiliate to one of 39 county associations, and players join Table Tennis England as members.
Tournaments are graded by stars, from one-star local events to four-star national ones.
England has its own teams at the World Championships; at the Olympics its players compete for Great Britain.
Sport England funds much of the domestic work, and UK Sport funds the Olympic and Paralympic programmes.
body: Table tennis in England is run by Table Tennis England, the national governing body. It runs national competitions, registers and insures players, qualifies coaches and umpires, and delivers England's performance programme. Below it are 39 county associations, more than 100 local leagues and the clubs where people actually play. Above it are the European and world federations, and, for the Olympics, a body that represents all four home nations together.
## Table Tennis England

The governing body dates its founding to 7 November 1921. It took the name English Table Tennis Association in 1927 and became Table Tennis England in May 2014. Legally it is still the English Table Tennis Association Ltd, a company limited by guarantee, which means it has no shareholders and no owner taking a profit. Its headquarters are at the National Badminton Centre in Milton Keynes.
Its members include players, clubs, leagues and county associations, and it is answerable to them through a National Council and a board.
## Counties, leagues and clubs

England is divided into 39 county associations. Every affiliated league and club must belong to the county that covers it. Counties have their own committees and run their own affairs, including county championships and county teams, which play each other, and Wales, in the national County Championships.

The local leagues are where most competitive table tennis happens. In the 2024-25 season Table Tennis England had 139 local leagues affiliated, plus four regional and county leagues. Each sets its own divisions, fixtures and local rules within the national regulations, and most play on weekday evenings through the winter. Clubs enter teams in their league, and the league registers each player.

Leagues keep their fixtures and results online. Table Tennis England offers its own system, TT Leagues, free to affiliated leagues, and many leagues use TT365, an independent platform. Our guide to [finding a club and joining a league](/guide/find-a-table-tennis-club-england.html) explains how to get into a team.
## Membership

Anyone who plays in an affiliated league or tournament must be a member of Table Tennis England. There were 29,307 members at the end of March 2025. For the 2026-27 season, which runs from 1 August to 31 July, there are four types.

Supporter and Club Play are free; Club Play adds public liability insurance for playing at your club. Compete, at £26 for adults, is the one you need for a local league, and it adds personal accident insurance, ratings and one-star tournaments. Compete Plus, at £49 for adults, is needed for national competitions and the British League. Under-19s pay less, and under-11s pay nothing at any level.
## Tournaments and national competitions

Individual tournaments are graded by stars. One-star events are local, two-star events regional and four-star events national. In 2026-27 there are five senior four-star events in England, in Liverpool, Sussex, Cleveland, Nottingham and Grantham. The National Championships, the top domestic individual event, are by invitation only.

The national team competitions are the British Clubs Leagues, which brought the old British League under one name in 2024-25. There are separate senior, veterans', junior and women's leagues, and in 2025-26 they had 846 teams and 4,397 players. Results in leagues and tournaments feed into the ratings and rankings lists that members appear on.
## Coaches and officials

From January 2026 Table Tennis England replaced its old coaching levels 1 to 4 with three qualifications: Coaching Assistant, Coach and Head Coach. Qualified coaches must hold Coach membership, which requires an enhanced DBS check and a safeguarding workshop, both renewed every three years, and a first aid qualification.
Umpires and referees have their own pathways, from level 1 up to international level. New umpires start on level 1 courses run through Technical Officials Academies.
## England, Great Britain and the world

England, Scotland and Wales each have their own governing body, and each is a separate member of the European Table Tennis Union (ETTU) and the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF). Northern Ireland plays as part of an all-Ireland association, through its Ulster branch. So England sends its own teams to the World Championships and the European Championships. Our guide to [the ITTF and WTT](/guide/ittf-and-wtt-explained.html) explains the world bodies.

At the Olympics there is no England team. GB Table Tennis, made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Ulster, nominates players to Team GB and invests the UK Sport funding meant to win Olympic medals. Our guide to [Olympic qualification](/guide/olympic-table-tennis-qualification.html) has the details.
At the Commonwealth Games England competes as Team England. Table tennis was not on the programme at Glasgow 2026, and Table Tennis England has said it will push for the sport's return from 2030.
## Where the money comes from

Much of Table Tennis England's work is paid for by the government through Sport England, whose long-term partnership is worth about £11.2m from 2022 to 2027. UK Sport funds elite performance: about £1.58m for Olympic table tennis in the cycle to the Los Angeles 2028 Games, with a further £206,000 announced in May 2026. It also funds para table tennis, which took most of the UK Sport money in Table Tennis England's accounts for 2025-26.
## Your next steps

If you want to start competing, read [how to find a club and join a league](/guide/find-a-table-tennis-club-england.html), then see how [team matches work](/guide/team-table-tennis-format.html). Our guide to [ratings and rankings for club players in England](/guide/table-tennis-england-ratings.html) explains what your results do to your number.
